source: TomorrowX Summit (iConnections) — Opening session: retail as most powerful market force, AI buildout railroad vs telecom, P(doom) vs P(boom)
summary: Retail investors are now the most powerful force in markets, displacing traditional sell-side research
summary_extended: Baker argues that retail investors have structurally displaced traditional sell-side research as the dominant force in equity markets, citing a specific crystallizing anecdote: a bulge bracket bank issued a strong sell downgrade with a massive price target cut on a semiconductor capital equipment stock, yet the stock rose 7% because a single line from a Substack/X account (Catrini) included it in a basket of names. He views this as not a one-off anomaly but a durable, structural shift in market power dynamics that he has been observing for six to seven years. The investment implication is that understanding and tracking retail sentiment flows — particularly through influential independent voices on social media and Substack — is now more alpha-generative than monitoring traditional sell-side research. This structural view motivated Baker to build TomorrowX, suggesting he sees a platform or information-aggregation opportunity in serving or harnessing this new retail-driven market dynamic.
